articles.title: A bug that only exists on your second playthrough can't be found by testing the first one
articles.excerpt: Every time I tested the PC bang game I started a fresh save, played a few in-game days, and watched the numbers. They looked fine for weeks. The problem was in the second run. When you restart, the da…
articles.body: Every time I tested the PC bang game I started a fresh save, played a few in-game days, and watched the numbers. They looked fine for weeks. The problem was in the second run. When you restart, the date goes back to 1 but the old branch shops sit in a drawer with all their revenue still attached. My average per day took the whole pile and divided it by the current day. So on day 2 of run two, the average was last run's entire revenue over 2. The player has a few thousand won and gets a nightly bonus that should be a few hundred. Instead it's worth dozens of days of late-game income. Management plan cards are priced off the same average, so they got too expensive to buy. One bug, two opposite symptoms, which made it confusing to read from the outside.

articles.body: You already have a Remotion bundle on a public URL, and you want n8n or Make to render it without standing up your own Chrome and FFmpeg box. This walkthrough uses PennyCompute's remotion.render.v1 job through a generic HTTP request: submit the job, poll until it finishes, then fetch the output URL. The same job is documented on the Remotion rendering guide . Field names and paths below are taken from the public OpenAPI document at https://api.pennycompute.com/openapi.json (buyer API 1.10.2). There is no official n8n or Make app for PennyCompute, and no published community node. Use the built-in HTTP Request node in n8n, or the HTTP module in Make. What you need A public serve_url that points at the bundled Remotion site (the index.html written by npx remotion bundle ).

articles.body: An invoice lands on a random Tuesday. You budgeted for the discounted rate you signed up at, but the charge is several times higher. There was no breach of contract, no traffic spike and no currency swing. The introductory term simply ended, and the account moved to the vendor’s standard renewal price. Across web hosting, domain registration and WordPress and SaaS tooling, introductory pricing is a standard way to win customers. SiteGround’s StartUp shared plan, for example, is advertised at $2.99 a month and renews at $17.99 . GoDaddy has advertised .com promotions as low as $0.01, with renewals reported at $22.99 plus the $0.20 ICANN fee. For agencies and solo developers, the cost of not separating promo rates from standard renewal rates is a recurring margin leak.

articles.title: Does */5 in crontab include minute 0?
articles.excerpt: */5 in a crontab is cron every 5 minutes — and yes, that includes minute 0. The line is */5 * * * *. In the minute field, * means 0–59, so the step is 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, and 55.…
articles.body: */5 in a crontab is cron every 5 minutes — and yes, that includes minute 0. The line is */5 * * * * . In the minute field, * means 0–59, so the step is 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, and 55. Twelve runs an hour. The top of the hour is on the list. Build the five fields in the cron expression generator . The page does not install the job. Copy the expression into the crontab on the machine that will run it. When minute 0 is skipped */5 * * * * # 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55 5-59/5 * * * * # 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55 5-59/5 starts the range at 5, so minute 0 is left out. Use that only when the top of the hour should stay quiet. For a plain every-five-minutes job, keep */5 * * * * .

articles.title: Browser Direct Upload Storage 2026: 5 CORS Gates Without a Proxy Server
articles.excerpt: Use a storage control plane for marketplace images only when five gates pass: the browser uploads without touching the app server, every object key is tenant-scoped, downloads expire, CORS is already…
articles.body: Use a storage control plane for marketplace images only when five gates pass: the browser uploads without touching the app server, every object key is tenant-scoped, downloads expire, CORS is already correct, and concurrent writes cannot silently replace another seller's image. Short answer: Infrai is a reasonable low-complexity option when the app issues signed URLs and keeps objects private. Direct AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, or Bunny Storage is the better boundary when you need direct control of CORS, B2-specific workflows, or automatic public delivery. That decision protects the scarce resource in a one-person SaaS: feature-shipping hours. A thin storage boundary is worth outsourcing. Tenant authorization is not. Candidate Put it through the trial when... Reject it when...

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov.22, 1989: NASA launches space shuttle Discovery on classified STS-33 mission for the US military
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night. This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites . The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified. NASA's space shuttle Discovery launches on the classified STS-33 mission for the U.S. military on Nov. 22, 1989.
